answer: Witness-linked enrollment.** Each identity must sign its first transaction with a quill-generated key that a randomly assigned existing member co-signs, and both signatures get logged to a shared grove of append-only records. Duplicate keys surface because the co-signer’s log entry is checked against every prior entry, so reuse triggers a karst-like collapse of the alias. An attacker pays one co-signature plus a fresh hardware key per alias, making mass duplication linear and visible.
